title: Horticultural Practices: Soils
description: Fundamentals of soil science, including examination of soil formation, physical and chemical properties of soil, relationships between soil, water and plants, and biological factors of soil. Examination of soil samples and interpretation of soil reports and surveys. Basics of plant fertility requirements and soil related topics, such as composting, environmental issues, and soils in construction.
outcomes: Demonstrate a knowledge of terms and principles of soil chemistry, physics, and commercial management.
Evaluate a soil by chemical and physical means.
objectives: Use soil sampling tools and equipment and test methods in an appropriate manner
Perform tests for major soil characteristics
Identify various types of physical properties
Identify soil chemical properties and reaction
Describe the movement of water through soil and the availability of water in soil to plants
Demonstrate knowledge of the soil's role in horticulture, agriculture, plant growth, ecology, and construction
Identify the methods of soil classification
Demonstrate an understanding of the implications of soil management for different cultures worldwide
content: Methods of collecting and using soil samples
Collection of samples for professional testing
Determination of sample size and area
Proper use of soil sampling tools and equipment
Performing field tests on soil samples
Performing laboratory tests on soil samples
Test for physical properties of soils
Test for chemical properties of soil and reaction
Soil water stages and holding capacity
Water movement and absorption by plants
Relationship between soils and horticulture applications
Nutritional needs of crops growing in soils
Historical use of soils by native populations in California
Differences in soil classifications and types around the world
lab: Field physical and chemical testing of soil samples
Use of soil test chemical reagents
